solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Smart boy spilling nothing when collecting water

indicators.note: the trimmed boy gathers the water into its middle, so it holds the other piece
spilling something means letting it out, so the zero is lost from the word

parts.note: taken as the word itself
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: A clever lad drops nothing even while catching rainwater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilling' looks like losing water, which fits the rainy picture, but it signals that the zero is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainy is an informal synonym for clever or intelligent, as smart is.

clue.text: Simple facts coming from arts graduates in charge of science initially!

parts.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts, holders of arts degrees

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word science

explanation.surface: An exclamation that even humanities graduates run the science basics.
explanation.definitionFit: The basics of a subject are its simplest, most fundamental facts.

clue.text: A quiet person saying 'Well done!'? Not necessarily, at work!

definitions.text: A quiet person saying 'Well done!'? Not necessarily, at work!

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
someone who says well done is one who praises, a praiser

explanation.surface: A muted praiser of others, who in fact only assesses things on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue builds A + P + PRAISER, then warns that this professional valuer does not necessarily praise anything: the whole clue is both wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An appraiser is someone whose job is to assess or value things, not necessarily favourably.

clue.text: Poor hen suffering, one very unfortunate

indicators.note: the letters are in a bad way, so they are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A poor hen in distress, an unlucky creature indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' looks like part of the picture of the hen but is fodder: POOR HEN rearranged under 'suffering'.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-hoper is a person with no chance of success, an unlucky loser.

clue.text: Unattached man fancied Chloe in the pub

indicators.note: the rearranged name goes inside the drinking place

parts.note: a bar is a pub or a room in one

indicators.note: fancied in the sense of fanciful, made up, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A single man had a crush on Chloe in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancied' reads as the man's attraction to Chloe but is the anagram signal; 'Unattached' means unmarried, not loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor is an unmarried man, one not attached to a partner.

clue.text: Minoan Crete, fantastic old civilisation

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly fanciful, so the letters are rearranged freely

explanation.surface: The Minoan culture of Crete as a marvellous ancient civilisation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the Minoans, another old civilisation, but MINOAN CRETE is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The classical Roman state is a famous civilisation of the ancient world.

clue.text: Water-containing chemical he has injected behind, going up!

indicators.note: the word he takes the other piece injected into its middle

parts.note: taken as the word itself

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word for late reads from bottom to top

parts.note: behind as in late, running behind, is tardy

explanation.surface: A chemical sample containing water is jabbed into someone's rear in a laboratory accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' turns only the word for late, giving YDRAT. 'behind' tempts as the backside; it means late.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydrate is a chemical compound containing combined water molecules.

clue.text: One serving lord, for instance, in story

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits inside the word for a tall tale

parts.note: a story is a lie, a fib
eg is the abbreviation for for instance (exempli gratia)

explanation.surface: A vassal appears, say, in a tale of feudal times.
explanation.walkthrough: Liege can mean either the lord or the vassal; here it is the vassal who serves.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege, or liegeman, is a feudal vassal bound to serve a lord.

clue.text: One visiting uncle making a recovery?

definitions.text: One visiting uncle making a recovery?

parts.words: One visiting uncle making a recovery?
parts.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker; someone visiting to recover a pawned item buys it back

explanation.surface: A relative visits an ailing uncle who is getting better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is British slang for a pawnbroker, and recovering pawned goods is redeeming them.
explanation.definitionFit: Redeeming pawned goods means buying them back, so one who does it fits the clue.

clue.text: Poet apparent in short demonstration

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the trimmed display word
short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a show is a demonstration or display
app. is the abbreviation of apparent, as in heir apparent

explanation.surface: A poet shows up in a brief demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparent' is shortened as in 'heir app.'; the poet is the Greek lyricist of Lesbos.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappho was an ancient Greek lyric poet from the island of Lesbos.

clue.text: Dad, I ache terribly — I must have a drug!

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly jumbled up

explanation.surface: A child tells their father of an awful pain and demands medication.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the cry of the person: an acid-head is an LSD user craving a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid-head is a habitual taker of LSD, someone craving that drug.

clue.text: Change map that's misprinted French place name

indicators.note: letters misprinted come out in the wrong order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Correcting a map with a misprinted name of a place in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is a region of north-east France, giving its name to the wine.

clue.text: You put in estimates for B&B establishments

indicators.note: the old pronoun is put into the middle of the word for estimates

parts.note: guesses are rough estimates
thou is the archaic form of you

explanation.surface: An instruction to enter estimates for bed-and-breakfast businesses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You' looks like an address to the reader but is the archaic pronoun; B&B is bed and breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Guesthouses are small private hotels, typically offering bed and breakfast.

clue.text: Woman taken in by bad element

indicators.note: the name is taken in by the phrase, held across its two words

explanation.surface: A woman is duped by a criminal type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' suggests being fooled, but it signals the name sitting inside 'bad element'.
explanation.definitionFit: Adele is a woman's first name.

clue.text: The way this drama goes on!

definitions.text: The way this drama goes on!

parts.words: The way this drama goes on!
parts.note: the way is a road, so the drama goes on in the road rather than on a stage

explanation.surface: A remark on how a play keeps unfolding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes on' looks like continues; it means is performed, and 'the way' is a street.
explanation.definitionFit: Street theatre is drama performed outdoors in public streets.

clue.text: Figures on targets getting shot

indicators.note: getting shot of something means being rid of it, and shot letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Numbers recorded on targets being fired at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figures' looks like scores on targets but means geometric shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetragons are four-sided plane figures, quadrilaterals.

clue.text: Newspaper features cuts (page inside)

indicators.note: the letter for page goes inside the word for cuts

parts.note: slashes are cuts

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about cuts, with a page of detail inside.
explanation.walkthrough: A newspaper splash is a prominent front-page story.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash is a sensational story given prominent display in a newspaper.

clue.text: Proficient set excited teacher demanding the best?

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An able group of pupils stirs up a teacher with high standards.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfectionist is someone who refuses to accept anything short of the best.

clue.text: Getting it wrong about a single item of jewellery?

indicators.note: about means the word goes round the other piece

parts.note: erring means making mistakes, getting it wrong
a single one is A

explanation.surface: Being mistaken about one piece of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: ERRING goes 'about' A. The question mark covers that an earring is one of a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: An earring is a piece of jewellery worn on the ear.

clue.text: Silly nerd — he and I were permanently stuck

indicators.note: silly suggests foolishness, so the letters are muddled up

explanation.surface: A complaint that a silly nerd, him and me were stuck together.
explanation.walkthrough: Inhere means to exist permanently in something.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhere is to be inherent, existing as a fixed part of something.

clue.text: Contact a person playing music, love getting trendy

parts.note: a DJ, disc jockey, plays recorded music
love is zero in tennis, like the letter O
in means fashionable, trendy

explanation.surface: Get in touch with a fashionable DJ who loves to play.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjoin is to be next to and touching, in contact with something.

clue.text: Hate being stuck in cab — horrible!

indicators.note: the word is stuck inside the phrase, across its two words

explanation.surface: A traveller hates being trapped in a taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor something is to hate or detest it.

clue.text: What's praised, not half — revolutionary country verse form

indicators.note: not half means only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: hailed means praised, acclaimed

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: Praise of a verse form from a country in revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: HAILED halved gives HAI, and the UK turned 'revolutionary' gives KU.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a Japanese verse form of three short lines.

clue.text: Picked up second bit of broadcast with external aerial?

indicators.note: external means the aerial word is placed outside the picked letter

parts.note: aerial means in the air, overhead

indicators.note: second bit of points to the second letter of the word broadcast

explanation.surface: Second part of a broadcast caught via an outdoor antenna.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aerial' looks like an antenna but is the adjective, OVERHEAD, round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Overheard means heard by chance, picked up without being meant to.

clue.text: The air is polluted — it's most dangerous

indicators.note: polluted means contaminated, so the letters are spoilt and rearranged

explanation.surface: Polluted air is the deadliest kind.
explanation.walkthrough: Hairy means dangerous or alarming, so hairiest is most dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairy is informal for frightening or risky, so the superlative means most dangerous.

clue.text: A river I love so comes into a piece of music

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A river that I love so much flows into a musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: An arioso is a melodious piece of vocal music, between aria and recitative.

clue.text: Most complacent dope gets sorted out by head of school

indicators.note: head of points to the first letter of school

parts.note: a mug is a dope, a fool

indicators.note: sorted out means reorganised, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A self-satisfied fool is dealt with by a headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: S from 'head of school', then MUG, then GEST from 'gets sorted out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug means self-satisfied or complacent; the superlative is most complacent.

clue.text: Journalist is performing, a very inventive man

parts.note: ed is short for editor, a journalist
taken as written
on means on stage, performing

explanation.surface: A journalist is performing as a great inventor.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Edison was the prolific American inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was a celebrated American inventor of the light bulb and phonograph.
